## NVIDIA–SK Group $500B alliance and Samsung–Broadcom $200B pact drive AI chip deal surge

The simultaneous announcement of two nine-figure AI chip alliances — with TSMC explicitly named as the competitive threat — signals that AI infrastructure capex is accelerating and that Korea's semiconductor complex is emerging as the primary alternative supply chain node; TSM's foundry moat warrants closer monitoring.

- Two major AI chip partnerships were announced in close proximity: NVIDIA and SK Group at $500B+, Samsung and Broadcom at $200B.
- Headlines explicitly frame both deals as part of an intensifying foundry race against TSMC.
- The Samsung–Broadcom deal extends through 2030 per one headline; NVDA–SK duration not specified in this cluster's coverage.
- TSMC is named as the competitive benchmark, framing these deals as market-share contest for advanced AI chip manufacturing.
- Arithmetic from stated headline figures puts the two deals' combined commitments at $700B+.
